chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Rooming houses, buses and hotels that would not take black musicians
summary: They discuss rooming houses full of bedbugs, travelling by bus and hotels that would not take black guests.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In a way, I guess it was better, when you were on the road in those days, to go to places like a rooming house, which was the sort of place where they catered to musicians, rather than going to a hotel like they do now, where you go to a hotel and it's probably more expensive, even by (?) standards.

Oh, it is. But those rooming houses weren't too hot either. A lot of places had a lot of bedbugs and things like that, you know -- and that's no fun! Yeah... I think hotels would have been better, because all the guys would have been together. At rooming houses and things like that, guys were scattered all over, you know....
Were most of you driving your own cars then, or was it on the bus...?
Well, then, it would be maybe a problem sometimes getting everybody to the job on time and getting everybody to the place on time...
Yeah, yeah. It was kind of rough that way. Yeah. Wherein if you just stayed at a hotel... But there was no hotels... The hotels wouldn't take no Colored at that
